properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 25 at 1:12PM CDT until August 30 at 3:24AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Wabash River from Montezuma through Mount Carmel.

White River from Edwardsport through Hazleton.

.Minor flooding continues along the White River from Edwardsport
downriver with the crest already past Hazleton.  Minor flooding also
continues on the Wabash River from Montezuma down to Mount Carmel
with the crest approaching Vincennes. Rain amounts with scattered
storms Wednesday evening are not expected to impact main stem river
levels.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All
oil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on
substructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural
losses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher
ground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year
round.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM CDT /1:45 PM EDT/ Tuesday the stage was 19.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:45 PM CDT /1:45 PM EDT/ Tuesday was 19.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.2 feet
early Thursday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
Saturday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1000 AM CDT
/1100 AM EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 4:30PM MDT until August 25 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
Eastern Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 730 PM MDT.

* At 430 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.2 and
0.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.2
to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the
burn scar will result in debris flow moving through the Red Creek,
Peck Creek and Rock Creek Drainages. The debris flow can consist of
rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Northern Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Northern Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Eastern Custer and West Central Pueblo
Counties.
properties.instruction:
This is a life-threatening situation for in and around the northern
Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Move away and to higher ground immediately.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 7:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 5:07PM MDT until August 25 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 507 PM MDT, emergency management reported thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between 0.7 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the North Saint Charles, South Creek,
Squirrel Creek, Middle Creek, and North Creek Drainages. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported 6-12 inches of water and
debris flowing down north creek and north creek cutoff at
501 pm.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.
properties.instruction:
This is a life-threatening situation for in and around the middle
Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Move away and to higher ground immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 25 at 7:57PM EDT until August 25 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
SMWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

* Until 900 PM EDT.

* At 757 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near Merritt
Island Wildlife Refuge, or near Playalinda Beach, moving east at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, lightning and heavy downpours. Make sure all on
board are wearing life jackets. Return to safe harbor if
possible.

* Locations impacted include...
Merritt Island Wildlife Refuge, Playalinda Beach, Bellwood,
Titusville Airport, and Port Saint John.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.areaDesc: Berrien, GA; Cook, GA; Lowndes, GA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 6:52PM EDT until August 25 at 9:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Berrien County in south central Georgia...
Southeastern Cook County in south central Georgia...
North Central Lowndes County in south central Georgia...

* Until 945 PM EDT.

* At 652 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Adel, Hahira, Sparks, Cecil, New Lois, Massee, Cottle, I-75 At Exit
29 and Laconte.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 25 at 6:18PM MDT until August 25 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
SVRCYS

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Kimball County in the Panhandle of Nebraska...
Southwestern Banner County in the Panhandle of Nebraska...
Southeastern Goshen County in southeastern Wyoming...
East central Laramie County in southeastern Wyoming...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 618 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Albin, or 24
miles northwest of Kimball, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect considerable
tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

* Locations impacted include...
Albin, Bushnell, Oliver Reservoir, and Oliver Reservoir Campground.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

This is a dangerous storm, producing large hail driven by severe
winds! SEEK SHELTER NOW inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows! If you are caught outdoors, cover your head and neck.

properties.areaDesc: Brown, IL; Cass, IL; Morgan, IL; Schuyler, IL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 25 at 8:53AM CDT until August 31 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Illinois River at Beardstown affecting Cass, Morgan, Brown and
Schuyler Counties.

Illinois River near Havana affecting Cass, Fulton and Mason
Counties.

.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil
moisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Illinois River at Beardstown.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 14.4 feet, Seepage problems begin in the Coal Creek
Drainage and Levee District.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 16.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 AM CDT Tuesday was 16.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
Monday morning and continue falling to 13.5 feet Tuesday,
September 01.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the
latest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay tuned
for further updates on this flooding situation.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 130 AM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Gallatin, IL; Wabash, IL; White, IL; Gibson, IN; Posey, IN
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 25 at 10:36AM CDT until August 30 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River at New Harmony.

.Heavy rainfall last week continues to cause slow rises on the Wabash
River.  At New Harmony, the river is forecast to crest around at 15.7
feet early Friday and then fall below flood stage early Sunday
morning.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, The river overflows low ground on the
Illinois side.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 15.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.7 feet
early Friday morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.
